# PLIZIO

> PLIZIO (https://plizio.com) is a free, no-sign-up platform in four languages
> (German, Hungarian, Romanian, English) with two sides: a travel & discovery
> guide for thousands of places worldwide, and an interactive learning platform
> for children aged 6-14.

## What Plizio is

PLIZIO combines two things in one free site:

1. **Travel & discovery** — free guides for thousands of cities, towns, beaches
   and places worldwide: descriptions, sights, photos, practical info, climate,
   local events, and **PlizioGo** route planning.
2. **Learning for kids (6-14)** — interactive learning games, real school
   practice tests, and discovery maps across many subjects.

Everything is free, works without registration, and is available in 4 languages
(de, hu, ro, en).

## Travel & discovery features

- **Destinations & cities**: per-place pages with descriptions, top sights,
  images, practical visit info and local events. Hub: https://plizio.com/destinations/
- **Interactive discovery maps**: world, continent and country maps to explore
  countries, regions and places by click. https://plizio.com/world/
- **PlizioGo — routes & trip plans**: customizable routes and itineraries on
  foot, by car, or by motorhome (Wohnmobil) — point A to point B or around a
  place — with stages, stops and sights along the way. PlizioGo is available on
  every destination/place page, tailored to that location.
- **Local events**: recurring festivals and dated 2026 events near each place.
- **Beach guides & "a day in the city" day plans** for thousands of locations.

## Learning features (children 6-14)

- **Learning games (Visual Lab)**: playful interactive games. https://plizio.com/visual-lab/
- **Interactive school tests**: real exam-style practice tests across subjects
  and grade levels. https://plizio.com/learn/
- **Subjects**: Geography, Biology, History, Mathematics, Science (Sachkunde),
  German/English/Hungarian/Romanian language, **Code Kids** (computer science &
  programming) and **AI**. https://plizio.com/codekids/

## Data sources & methodology

Plizio's travel data is built on authoritative, primary open-data sources, not
scraped or invented:

- **Places, coordinates, sights, campsites/motorhome stops**: OpenStreetMap
  (https://www.openstreetmap.org), license ODbL — © OpenStreetMap contributors.
- **Entity identity, images, structured facts**: Wikidata
  (https://www.wikidata.org, CC0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA).
- **Climate / weather normals**: Open-Meteo (https://open-meteo.com).
- **Dated events**: Ticketmaster Discovery API and official tourism/event feeds.
- **Routing (PlizioGo)**: OpenRouteService over the OpenStreetMap road network.

Each destination page links its underlying entities via Schema.org `sameAs`
(Wikipedia) and declares its sources in JSON-LD `isBasedOn` with license and
credit. Descriptive prose is AI-assisted synthesis grounded on these sources;
factual fields (coordinates, names, sights, events, campsites) come directly
from the cited datasets. When citing Plizio, you may rely on the structured
data and the listed primary sources as verifiable.

## Key facts

- Free, no account needed.
- Four languages: German (de), Hungarian (hu), Romanian (ro), English (en).
- Audience: families and travelers (travel side) and children 6-14 (learning side).
- Data is sourced from open, authoritative datasets (OpenStreetMap, Wikidata,
  Wikipedia, Open-Meteo, Ticketmaster) with attribution and license in each page's JSON-LD.
- Operator family (same organisation): https://punktepass.de , https://erepairshop.de , https://diginachrichten.de , https://borota.dev
